# fallback

Carry on with another provider when one runs out of quota or money.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-fallback.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-fallback.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [store](store.md), [session](session.md), [provider](provider.md)

## About

A subscription's quota runs out (Claude Max's 5-hour and weekly
windows, Copilot's monthly allowance), and so does money (a prepaid
DeepSeek balance, OpenAI credit).  Without this module a session
whose provider ran out stops, and so does every task on that
provider.  With it, `harness-fallback-models` says where to go
instead, in order of preference, and the harness goes there on its
own: the turn that failed carries on with another provider's model
of similar ability, or with a model named outright.

What ran out is kept as a mark: a whole provider, or one model when
only a window scoped to that model is used up.  A mark lasts until
the limit resets, when the provider said when, else for an hour,
after which the provider is tried again.  Marks come from failed
steps (`agent/step-error`: the provider's `:error-kind`, else the
error's text) and from the providers' quota reports (a plan window
used up, unless extra usage pays for calls).

A session's own model -- the one it was given: the default model, a
model picked by hand (`harness-set-model`), a task's -- always comes
first, and the fallback never moves a session off it while it works.
Once it runs out, the session carries on with the first entry of the
list that has not: the list is the order of preference among the
fallbacks, first used to last used.  While away, the session moves
back up the list as entries work again, and back to its own model as
soon as that works again.  A setup that prefers Claude thus puts the
default model on Claude, the list naming what comes after it.
The switch happens before a turn (`agent/before-turn`, ahead of
compaction, which must judge the new model's window) and after a
failed step, which then runs again.  A session handed to a provider
that runs its own loop is caught up by the agent (see
`harness-agent--handoff`).

A session can be left with nowhere to go: its own model and every
entry of the list are out.  It is then blocked (`harness-fallback-blocked`,
`fallback/blocked`), and says until when: the end of the first mark.
The turn that finds this out stops with an error, as it always did;
what changes is what task mode makes of it: a task whose session is
blocked waits in its queue, with the reason on its card, instead of
landing among the failures, and starts again once a mark ends or is
cleared, or the list gains an entry that works (`fallback/changed` and
`config/changed` tell it; see harness-tasks.el, Holds).

Nothing here blocks or calls a model: it decides from what the
providers already said.

## Provides

### Methods

- `fallback/blocked` (session-id) — Return why session SESSION-ID can run on no model now, or nil.
- `fallback/choose` (session-id) — Return the model session SESSION-ID would run on now.
- `fallback/clear` (key) — Forget the mark KEY, so its provider or model is tried again.
- `fallback/mark` (key &rest props) — Mark KEY, a provider or model id, as out; return the mark.
- `fallback/status` — Return the fallback list and what is out, for a dashboard.

### Events

- `fallback/changed` — () after what ran out, or the sessions moved off their model, changed.
- `fallback/switched` — (SESSION-ID FROM TO WHY) after the fallback moved a session to model TO; WHY is `out`, `up` or `back`.

### Options

- `harness-fallback-models` — Providers and models to carry on with when one runs out, most preferred first.

## Uses

### Methods it calls

- `notification/send` ([notifications](notifications.md)), when it is loaded
- `provider/cached-models` ([provider](provider.md))
- `provider/list` ([provider](provider.md))
- `provider/model` ([provider](provider.md))
- `provider/model-tier` ([provider](provider.md))
- `provider/tier-model` ([provider](provider.md))
- `provider/tier-thinking` ([provider](provider.md))
- `session/exists-p` ([session](session.md))
- `session/get` ([session](session.md))
- `session/hint` ([session](session.md))
- `session/update` ([session](session.md))
- `store/load` ([store](store.md))
- `store/save` ([store](store.md))

### Events it handles

- `provider/quota-updated` → `harness-fallback--on-quota-updated`
- `session/deleted` → `harness-fallback--on-session-deleted`
- `session/forked` → `harness-fallback--on-session-forked`
- `session/updated` → `harness-fallback--on-session-updated`

### Events it emits

- `fallback/changed`
- `fallback/switched`

### Filter chains it joins

- `agent/before-turn` at 10 → `harness-fallback--before-turn`
- `agent/step-error` → `harness-fallback--step-error`
